newsitem.title: SYRIA: Eight Arab states to discuss forming common market.
newsitem.headline: Eight Arab states to discuss forming common market.

text.p: Foreign ministers from eight Arab states open talks in the Syrian Mediterranean city of Latakia on Wednesday, with the establishment of an Arab common market high on the agenda.

Officials said Syria, Egypt and the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would also discuss Turkey's incursion in northern Iraq against separatist Kurds, Ankara's ties with Israel and voice their backing for Syria against Israel.
Officials said Syria would support the establishment of an Arab economic common market with Egypt and the GCC -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.
"It is strange that Arab states who have many things in common have the largest share of the trade with the outside world. This should not continue," one official said.

Egyptian officials say the government, seeking new export opportunities to shrink its huge trade deficit, has been galvanised into drafting proposals for the market which Egypt has enthusiastically adopted.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has touted the idea in almost all his major speeches recently and particularly after he visited neighbouring Libya.

Egypt's partnership accord with the European Union is linked to agricultural exports, while Israel's right-wing government, which has halted peace talks, has killed all hope of setting up a regional market soon.
Egyptian officials envisage a pan-Arab market including all countries in the region, but Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters it was willing to settle for a few members initially.
"Not all countries have to become members, but membership should be open to all," he said.

The ministers of the so-called Damascus Declaration, formed by countries that took part in a U.S.-led force that drove Iraqi forces from Kuwait in 1991, would also discuss Turkey's incursion into northern Iraq against the Kurds and its military cooperation with Israel, which has also raised concern among the Arab states.

Officials said Egypt and the GCC states would voice support for Syria's demands for a pledge by Israel to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights as a condition for resuming their peace talks, suspended for over a year.
Gulf diplomats said Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Abdullah would visit Syria on Wednesday for talks with President Hafez al-Assad aimed at supporting Syria's stand.
Israel broke off peace talks with Syria over a year ago and no talks have been held since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office last June.
Syria, which wants Israel to withdrawal fully from the Golan Heights, captured in 1967, has condemned Netanyahu for refusing to swap occupied Arab lands for peace.
Diplomats said a controversial Middle East economic conference including Israel, that Qatar is going to host in September, would not be discussed as a separate issue during the meeting.

But they said other members would stress the need to abide by resolutions adopted by an Arab summit in Cairo last year calling for a boycott of Israel if no progress was made in its peace talks with Arabs.

Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, who will chair the Latakia meeting, toured Arab states recently to rally support for the boycott of the Qatar conference.
Qatar has said it would go ahead with the meeting while other GCC states including powerful Saudi Arabia signalled they would not take part.
